title: Structured service request and error logs

steps.title: Declare the boundary: Structured service request and error logs

blocks.text: An interpretable event log says when and where an event happened, its type and severity, and enough context to understand the outcome.
For a failure, use consistent field names for timestamp, application or code location, event type, severity, result status and reason—not just unexplained free text.

logger.error(message, extra=event_fields) attaches fields to the LogRecord. Configure the existing formatter or collector to preserve their names, and avoid custom keys that collide with reserved LogRecord attributes.

before.code:
import io
import logging
captured_output = io.StringIO()
logger = logging.getLogger('order.failure.exercise')
logger.handlers.clear()
logger.propagate = False
logger.setLevel(logging.ERROR)
existing_handler = logging.StreamHandler(captured_output)
existing_handler.setFormatter(logging.Formatter('%(message)s'))
logger.addHandler(existing_handler)
failure_values = {
    'timestamp': '2026-01-01T12:00:00Z',
    'code_location': 'orders.create_order',
    'event_type': 'order_failure',
    'event_severity': 'error',
    'result_status': 'failed',
    'reason': 'synthetic stock unavailable',
}
reserved_attributes = sorted(set(logging.makeLogRecord({}).__dict__) | {'message', 'asctime'})

logger.error('failed')
print(captured_output.getvalue(), end='')

import io
import logging
captured_output = io.StringIO()
logger = logging.getLogger('order.failure.exercise')
logger.handlers.clear()
logger.propagate = False
logger.setLevel(logging.ERROR)
existing_handler = logging.StreamHandler(captured_output)
existing_handler.setFormatter(logging.Formatter('%(message)s'))
logger.addHandler(existing_handler)
failure_values = {
    'timestamp': '2026-01-01T12:00:00Z',
    'code_location': 'orders.create_order',
    'event_type': 'order_failure',
    'event_severity': 'error',
    'result_status': 'failed',
    'reason': 'synthetic stock unavailable',
}
reserved_attributes = sorted(set(logging.makeLogRecord({}).__dict__) | {'message', 'asctime'})

event_fields = dict(failure_values)
existing_handler.setFormatter(logging.Formatter('timestamp=%(timestamp)s code_location=%(code_location)s event_type=%(event_type)s event_severity=%(event_severity)s result_status=%(result_status)s reason=%(reason)s'))
logger.error('order failure', extra=event_fields)
print(captured_output.getvalue(), end='')

blocks.change_summary: Before: unexplained message. After: preserve the six named failure fields through the existing formatter. Emitted output is computed, not an observed production event.

blocks.text: Follow the fields from event_fields into the LogRecord and then into the emitted record. Use timestamp, code location, event type, severity, result status and reason consistently. Passing extra is not enough: inspect the existing formatter or collector to ensure those names survive. Custom names must not collide with reserved LogRecord attributes.

import io
import logging
captured_output = io.StringIO()
logger = logging.getLogger('order.failure.exercise')
logger.handlers.clear()
logger.propagate = False
logger.setLevel(logging.ERROR)
existing_handler = logging.StreamHandler(captured_output)
existing_handler.setFormatter(logging.Formatter('%(message)s'))
logger.addHandler(existing_handler)
failure_values = {
    'timestamp': '2026-01-01T12:00:00Z',
    'code_location': 'orders.create_order',
    'event_type': 'order_failure',
    'event_severity': 'error',
    'result_status': 'failed',
    'reason': failure_reason,
}
reserved_attributes = sorted(set(logging.makeLogRecord({}).__dict__) | {'message', 'asctime'})
import logging
# TODO: copy the six failure values into event_fields and preserve their
# names in the existing formatter. Emit logger.error(..., extra=event_fields).
event_fields = {
    'timestamp': failure_values['timestamp'],
    'code_location': failure_values['code_location'],
    'event_type': failure_values['event_type'],
    'event_severity': failure_values['event_severity'],
    'result_status': failure_values['result_status'],
    'reason': failure_values['reason'],
}
existing_handler.setFormatter(logging.Formatter('timestamp=%(timestamp)s code_location=%(code_location)s event_type=%(event_type)s event_severity=%(event_severity)s result_status=%(result_status)s reason=%(reason)s'))
logger.error('failed', extra=event_fields)
